text: On that day the LORD will punish with his sword—harsh, great, and mighty—Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the coiling serpent, and he will slay the dragon that is in the sea.
On that day: Sing of a delightful vineyard!
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it every moment. Lest anyone harm it, I guard it night and day.
I have no wrath. If only there were briers and thorns confronting me! I would march against them in battle, I would burn them up together.

versions.text: I have no wrath. If only there were briers and thorns to fight against me! I would march against them, I would burn them up together.
versions.explanation: בַּמִּלְחָמָה ("in battle") belongs with the marching clause rather than being converted into "to fight against me," which leaves the second clause weakened and drops an element of the Hebrew.

text: Or let them take hold of my stronghold and make peace with me—let them make peace with me.
In days to come Jacob will take root, Israel will bud and blossom, and fill the whole world with fruit.
Has he struck them as he struck the ones who struck them? Has he slain them as he slew their slayers?

versions.text: Has the LORD struck them as he struck the one who struck them? Has he slain them as he slew their slayers?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; inserting "the LORD" adds content not in the text, and the singular "the one who struck them" clashes with the plural "their slayers" in the parallel line.

text: Measure by measure he contended with them, driving them into exile; with his fierce blast he swept them away, as on a day of the east wind.

versions.text: By expelling, by driving them away, he contended with them; with his fierce blast he swept them off, as on a day of the east wind.
versions.explanation: The rare word בְּסַאסְּאָה is most commonly understood as "measure by measure" (a measured, proportionate judgment); rendering it as "by expelling" duplicates בְּשַׁלְחָהּ ("by sending/exiling her") and produces a redundant, awkward doublet for oral reading.

text: So then, this is how Jacob's guilt will be atoned for, and this the full fruit of the removal of his sin: when he smashes the altar stones to pieces like crumbling chalk, and no Asherah poles or incense altars are left standing.
For the fortified city stands desolate, an abandoned settlement, forsaken like the wilderness. There the calf grazes, there it lies down and strips its branches bare.

When its boughs are dry, they are broken off; women come and light their fires with them. For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no mercy.
On that day the LORD will thresh out the grain from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt, and you, people of Israel, will be gathered one by one.
On that day a great trumpet will sound, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those scattered in the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

versions.text: On that day a great trumpet will sound, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those driven away to the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew preposition is בְּאֶרֶץ ("in the land of"), parallel to the preceding phrase; "driven away to" changes location into direction and breaks the parallelism.
